descriptions.text: Chiyome. Razor Fox. Level 80 Mistress of Nunchaku. One of three from team The Wild Hunt. Since this is the first time you've examined a Razor Fox that wasn't suffering from an anatomy-changing disease, let me tell you about these little fellas. (And, ladies, since the one you're looking at is a lady ninja, they make the women ninjas wear red because . . . Well, I'm not sure why.) I love these guys. Each one picks a weapon proficiency upon childhood, kinda like a ninja-turtle thing, and they train in both that and in a ranged weapon. Most, like Chiyome here, pick throwing stars as their ranged weapon of choice.

beats.headline: Meeting the neighbours
beats.text: Carl and Donut come out of their garage into the Team Roundabout and go round the neighbours, which on this floor means meeting the NPCs who will be trying to survive the same heats. Among them, three Razor Foxes racing as The Wild Hunt, and the one doing the talking is Chiyome. Level eighty. Nunchaku on the belt and throwing stars beside them. I say on the record that I am fond of Razor Foxes. I do not say that about a species very often.

beats.headline: In on the plan
beats.text: Chiyome sits in on the plan with Carl, Donut, Radoslav and Jasha: Rapture into Donut's sights, one shot, done with it. It comes apart before a trigger is touched, because Team Sparkles destroys team Girth the Trouble's vehicle and Girth the Trouble is gone off this floor. Chiyome does not complain about the wasted planning, which puts her ahead of most of the field on this course and all of the commentary.

beats.headline: The Wild Hunt is eliminated
beats.text: Chiyome reported over the channel that The Wild Hunt was in trouble. Then sugar hermits began falling out of the sky, and Crawler Donut pulled Temporary Macaroni out of her Banquet Fit for a Princess and built a tunnel of it, and Crawler Carl got on the channel to tell Chiyome where to drive. There was no longer anybody to tell. The Wild Hunt is eliminated. The Jugglers with them. The tunnel was a good idea, arriving in the order that good ideas usually arrive in.
